source.table: National Weather Service heat index categories
source.verified: Chart read by hand: the chart is an image and could not be machine-read. Confirm the boundaries and wording against the NWS chart before relying on them.

bands.name: Below caution
bands.action: Below the heat index of 80 F where OSHA's extra heat precautions start. Drink water as usual.

bands.name: Caution
bands.effects: Fatigue is possible with long exposure or activity.
bands.action: Extra heat precautions apply from 80 F (OSHA). Drink water about every 15 minutes. Take rest breaks in the shade.

bands.name: Extreme caution
bands.rest: Frequent rest breaks in the shade.
bands.effects: Heat cramps, heat exhaustion or heat stroke are possible with long exposure or activity.
bands.action: Drink water about every 15 minutes. Take frequent rest breaks in the shade. Watch the crew for heat illness signs.

bands.name: Danger
bands.rest: Frequent rest breaks in the shade.
bands.effects: Heat cramps and heat exhaustion are likely. Heat stroke is probable with continued activity.
bands.action: Drink water about every 15 minutes. Take frequent rest breaks in the shade. Do the heaviest work in the cooler hours.

bands.name: Extreme danger
bands.rest: Frequent rest breaks in the shade.
bands.action: Move work out of these hours where you can. Where you cannot, drink water about every 15 minutes and take frequent rest breaks in the shade.

water_plan.name: Below caution
water_plan.action: Below the heat index of 80 F where OSHA's extra heat precautions start. Drink water as usual.

source.verified: Taken from NIOSH and OSHA pages as summarised by a search tool on 2026-10-18. Confirm against the pages before relying on it.

acclimatization.who: OSHA treats workers as unacclimatized when they have been on the job less than 1 to 2 weeks. NIOSH treats workers back after an absence of more than a week as new.

new.label: New workers
new.unit: percent of the usual time in the heat

experienced.label: Experienced workers, first days back
experienced.unit: percent of the usual time in the heat

notes: New workers start at no more than 20% of the usual time in the heat on day 1 and add no more than 20% each day.
Supervise new workers closely for the first 14 days or until they are fully acclimatized.
In a sudden heat wave, even experienced workers start the first hot day at 50% of the usual time.
For intense work, take frequent rest breaks and do the work in the cooler part of the day (OSHA).
The heat index assumes shade. In full sun it can be up to 15 F higher (NWS), so the sun column shows the upper case.
Hourly values are the highest of seven forecast points within 20 km of the site.
WBGT is an approximation and its tiers are not verified against TB MED 507.
OSHA treats workers as unacclimatized when they have been on the job less than 1 to 2 weeks. Use the acclimatization switch.

hazard_index.top_driver_text: flash flood, flood or heavy rain
caveats: The score is the chance that NOAA records a severe event of that kind near the plant, weighted by how often OSHA injuries follow. It is not a count of injuries.
The model was trained on 60 power plants and on reanalysis weather, then scored on live forecasts.
In tests the fire model did not beat a simple seasonal average. Do not act on a fire driver alone.
